authority.alpha_prerequisite: Provide the first executable H-05a prerequisite for OBJ-09 and OBJ-10: one kernel-owned, deterministic signal catalogue that later build identity, public projections, diagnostic runtimes, SDKs, and release evidence can consume without duplicating trace or metric semantics.

current_behavior: rrd-core already owns the closed TraceBoundary, TraceOperation, and TraceAttribute catalogues and validates durable trace evidence while depending only on serde. The architecture separately names four runtime diagnostic levels, twenty-two metric instruments, their kinds and units, nine permitted low-cardinality metric dimensions, and a default 2,000-point cardinality limit. No Rust telemetry module, metric descriptor catalogue, deterministic signal fingerprint, or checked-in machine projection exists. Current crates can therefore invent metric names, units, dimensions, or diagnostic levels independently, and the later build identity has no canonical signal-catalogue digest to bind. The root workspace also lacks the release-derived diagnostic profile and executable build identity, but those depend on this stable signal fingerprint and are intentionally deferred to the next H-05a packages.
target_behavior: Add one dependency-free rrd-core telemetry contract that derives trace-operation descriptors directly from TraceOperation::ALL and trace-attribute descriptors directly from TraceAttribute::ALL, owns the four diagnostic levels and the exact twenty-two architecture-defined metric descriptors, admits only the nine architecture-defined low-cardinality metric dimensions, validates canonical-order/uniqueness/name/kind/unit/dimension invariants, and computes one deterministic SHA-256 signal-catalogue fingerprint over a versioned unambiguous byte preimage. Export the types and constants from rrd-core and add a generated golden JSON projection plus negative and mutation-sensitive tests. The catalogue describes signal identity only: it emits no metric, reads no clock or environment, installs no subscriber, chooses no exporter, captures no content, and changes no authoritative runtime event. This package is H-05a slice 1 only; it does not claim H-05a or H-05 complete.
unchanged_behavior: README.md remains product identity and status owner; the objective owns measurable outcomes; the roadmap owns dependency and completion; the POA&M owns deficiency status; engine-data-flow remains the accepted signal contract.

TraceOperation, TraceBoundary, and TraceAttribute remain the only durable trace name/type owners. telemetry.rs must iterate their ALL catalogues and must not copy operation or trace-attribute strings into a second list.

RuntimeTraceEvent persistence, validation, direct-convergence inventories, engine execution, storage formats, query/index behavior, authorization, receipts, public operations, SDKs, and all current call sites remain byte- and behavior-compatible.

rrd-core retains serde as its only normal dependency. No tracing, OpenTelemetry, metrics SDK, exporter, async runtime, transport, storage, provider, model, profiler, or hosted service enters the kernel.

Cargo release/diagnostic/runtime-analysis/benchmark profiles, compile-time source/toolchain identity, executable and distribution digests, format/configuration identities, rrflow version, release/diagnostic parity, runtime level activation, overhead measurement, W3C propagation, exporters, and captures remain subsequent H-05a through H-05e work.

The telemetry catalogue types only interoperable signal/effect metadata. It does not encode exploratory reasoning, hypotheses, prompts, source bodies, model output, private analysis, or lifecycle state.
Product version remains 1.0.0. No roadmap checkbox, POA&M state, maturity, benchmark, release, or promotion claim changes.

implementation_changes.action: Expose the new kernel-owned signal catalogue through the existing rrd-core public boundary without changing or aliasing existing trace exports.
implementation_changes.failure_semantics: Stop if the public export requires an outward crate, renames an existing contract, or makes a diagnostic projection authoritative.

implementation_changes.action: Create the sole kernel semantic owner for diagnostic levels, trace-operation/attribute projection, metric instruments, kinds, units, permitted dimensions, validation, canonical versioned digest preimage, and SHA-256 fingerprint. Trace descriptors must be derived from TraceOperation::ALL and TraceAttribute::ALL, and every collection must be statically bounded and deterministic.
implementation_changes.failure_semantics: Reject unknown, duplicate, or out-of-canonical-order names; a trace operation whose name and boundary disagree; a metric descriptor with a wrong kind/unit or an undeclared, duplicate, or out-of-canonical-order dimension; an empty or noncanonical token; a cardinality limit other than the architecture-owned default for v1; and any digest computed from ambiguous or non-versioned concatenation.

implementation_changes.action: Add the pretty canonical JSON projection generated from SignalCatalogue, including its deterministic digest, for later contract/SDK/build-identity consumers and cross-language drift detection.
implementation_changes.failure_semantics: The fixture must be a replaceable projection from Rust catalogue code, not a manually interpreted authority; any byte or semantic drift fails until intentionally regenerated and reviewed.

implementation_changes.action: Author the failing contract oracle first, then prove exact architecture counts and values, derivation from TraceOperation::ALL and TraceAttribute::ALL, stable fixture bytes/digest, validation rejection for schema and catalogue drift, and no runtime/exporter authority.
implementation_changes.failure_semantics: The test must fail for a copied or missing trace operation, extra dynamic metric dimension, reordered descriptor, wrong unit/kind, unknown JSON field, stale fixture, unchanged digest after semantic mutation, or added normal kernel dependency.

evidence_changes.action: Create the H-05a slice-1 receipt with baseline/planning commit, full reads, test-first failure, exact catalogue/digest behavior, commands and results, surfaced failures, omissions, remaining H-05a work, and explicit no-status-change statement.
Regenerate the nearest Gate H journal index so the bounded implementation receipt is discoverable.
Regenerate the deterministic Git-backed path/digest inventory after the source, fixture, test, and evidence files exist.

research.reason: The preceding reviewed deep-research record resolved the portable semantics before this implementation plan. This package uses only its current primary-source conclusions needed for metric kinds/units, deterministic aggregation, bounded cardinality, and telemetry failure isolation; it adds no upstream code or public compatibility surface.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Metrics Data Model
sources.retained_behavior: Represent the closed catalogue with aggregatable counters, up/down counters, observable gauges, histograms, explicit units, and stable identifying attributes.
sources.rejected_assumption: Metric points or exporter output are authoritative engine state, and precomputed averages preserve useful distributions.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Metrics API
sources.retained_behavior: Use stable instrument descriptors and treat name, kind, unit, and description as one registration identity.
sources.rejected_assumption: Callers may dynamically create semantically conflicting instruments or unrestricted attributes.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Metrics SDK
sources.retained_behavior: Keep cardinality and aggregation controls explicit and ensure later SDK/exporter behavior is a replaceable projection of the semantic catalogue.
sources.rejected_assumption: An exporter-specific view or silent overflow policy may become the metric contract.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Error Handling
sources.retained_behavior: Keep diagnostic collection nonessential to application semantics and expose bounded telemetry failures separately.
sources.rejected_assumption: Signal creation or export failure may fail, retry, commit, roll back, or relabel an RRFlow engine operation.

sources.title: Prometheus Instrumentation Practices
sources.retained_behavior: Model work, latency, errors, queues, caches, and saturation with deliberately bounded dimensions.
sources.rejected_assumption: Request, project, record, path, provider, model, or arbitrary error values are safe metric labels.

runtime_trace.reason: TraceOperation::ALL and TraceAttribute::ALL are read as the sole durable trace-name sources for descriptor projections and the digest. RuntimeTraceEvent, durable trace persistence, direct-convergence names, call sites, clocks, spans, and causal behavior remain unchanged.

resource_evidence.reason: Add only the static identity of the twenty-two architecture-owned metric instruments and permitted dimensions. This package records no runtime sample, allocation, latency, throughput, or performance claim and adds no collection dependency.

debugging_evidence.reason: Add the closed off/normal/detailed/profile vocabulary and signal fingerprint needed by future build/capture identities. This package does not activate a level, retain symbols, capture data, or add a debug-only behavior.

first_failure_oracle: At baseline, crates/kernel/rrd-core/src/telemetry.rs, fixtures/telemetry-catalogue-v1.json, and tests/telemetry_contract.rs do not exist, and rrd-core exports no DiagnosticLevel, MetricInstrument, MetricDescriptor, SignalCatalogue, or signal-catalogue digest.

The architecture defines twenty-two exact instruments and nine permitted low-cardinality dimensions, but repository search finds no executable Rust owner for those names, kinds, units, relationships, or the default 2,000-point limit.
The root Cargo manifest has no custom profile and no build-identity implementation exists; those are intentionally not solved until this package supplies a stable signal-catalogue digest.

Baseline cargo test -p rrd-core --locked -- --list compiled successfully and listed the current 51 unit tests plus existing golden/integration tests, with no telemetry contract test. During implementation, author telemetry_contract.rs first and retain its expected unresolved-import/absent-fixture failure before adding telemetry.rs.

stop_conditions: Implementing the catalogue requires a normal rrd-core dependency beyond serde, an outward crate, a runtime clock/environment read, a global subscriber, exporter, storage access, network capability, provider, or model integration.

The implementation copies TraceOperation or TraceAttribute names instead of deriving them from their ALL catalogues, changes RuntimeTraceEvent or an existing operation/attribute, or creates a second operation, lifecycle, evidence, or telemetry authority.

A metric admits an estate, project, actor, session, request, trace, span, query, record, file/path, provider, model, collection, index generation, routine/job, error message, user value, prompt, source body, vector, credential, token, header, stack trace, or hidden reasoning as a metric dimension or payload.

The digest preimage is ambiguous, unversioned, process/order dependent, derived from debug formatting, or insensitive to a semantic change in trace operations, trace attributes, diagnostic levels, descriptors, units, kinds, dimensions, or cardinality policy.
The golden fixture becomes a handwritten authority, a normal test silently rewrites it, unknown fields deserialize successfully, or an invalid/duplicate/reordered catalogue is accepted.

The package expands into rrd-contract/OpenAPI/SDK projection, Cargo profiles, build scripts, version CLI, runtime instrumentation, W3C propagation, metrics SDK/export, capture, benchmarks, or release evidence without a new planning-only commit.
Any undeclared path changes, Cargo.lock drifts, an existing test regresses, documentation/navigation/inventory drifts, product version changes, or H-05/POAM-026/alpha completion is claimed.
